summary.text: Tamara Lesnar of Grenville, a Libertarian who runs a small collectibles business, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Secretary of State of South Dakota to Heather Baxter.
A former compliance officer at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, she ran for U.S. Senate in 2022 and the state House in 2024.
She supported continuing to use vote-tabulation machines and proposed online databases letting residents indicate preferences on issues before lawmakers vote.

paragraphs.text: Lesnar worked as a compliance officer at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and now operates a small collectibles business in Grenville.
She was the Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senate in South Dakota in 2022, receiving 4% of the vote, and ran unsuccessfully for the South Dakota House in 2024.
The Libertarian Party of South Dakota nominated Lesnar for secretary of state, and her campaign said she promised to protect civil liberties and civil rights.

Her platform listed easier access to voting locations, curbing double taxation, a statewide database for ballot initiatives and signatures, and filing lawsuits against laws that violate the Bill of Rights.
She received 5.5% of the vote to Heather Baxter's 58.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
